cohort_name: unnamed: Oxford Academic Health Science Network mental health services (Thames Valley and South Midlands, England), 2010-2011
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 F20, F22 or F25 recorded as a primary or secondary diagnosis in the Mental Health Minimum Data Set, PLUS a psychosis-related Mental Healthcare Cluster (10-17, Mental Health Clustering Tool), PLUS reported problems with hallucinations and delusions (HONOS Working Age Adults item 6)
diagnosis_confirmed: Administrative record only; no research diagnostic interview. The identification algorithm 'was developed with clinical experts and service leaders, and validated by analyses performed in 3 (of 15) AHSNs in England' and returned 15,709 patients against 17,993 in Quality and Outcomes Framework data.
overlap_notes: Regional linkage of Hospital Episode Statistics and the Mental Health Minimum Data Set across four Mental Health Trusts. No overlap with any other F13 cohort. Possible overlap with any other report drawing on English MHMDS 2010-2013 for the same region.
employment_selection_verbatim: 'Patients were identified with psychosis if they (1) had a primary or secondary diagnosis of psychosis (ICD-10 codes: F20 schizophrenia, F22 persistent delusional disorders or F25 schizoaffective disorders), (2) were classified into one of the Mental Healthcare Clusters related with psychosis (clusters 10-17, using the Mental Health Clustering Tool) and (3) reported problems associated with hallucination and delusions (question 6 from Health of the Nation Outcome Scale (HONOS) in the HONOS Working Age Adults Questionnaire). ... We further restricted the sample to patients in the age group of 16-35 years with an observed HONOS score at 2010/2011, which resulted in 3674 patients.' The complete recruitment chain is stated and contains no employment-related criterion at any step.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Patient sample, p. 2. NOTE: 'A detailed description of the sample selection criteria and sample identification is presented in online supplementary appendix 1', which is not held in this repository; the classification rests on the main-text chain, which is complete as printed. See unresolved_queries.md Q1.

cohort_name: DETECT early intervention for psychosis service two-pronged vocational study, Dublin
diagnostic_instrument: 'A standardized assessment protocol was conducted to ascertain diagnosis and clinical presentation' at the EIPS; the instrument is not named in this report and is deferred to Renwick et al. (2015). Diagnoses were grouped into schizophrenia/schizophreniform, affective psychosis/schizoaffective, and other psychotic illness.
diagnosis_confirmed: Clinical assessment at the early intervention service; instrument not named here.
overlap_notes: Same service and same vocational programme as Turner, O'Callaghan and Clarke (2016), the matched historical-control study, which is not held. The historical control group in that study is a different sample from this one.
employment_selection_verbatim: 'The SES offered the appropriate intervention to all those internally referred to them.' ... 'In total, 129 people were offered the interventions ... 64 accepted of whom 61 used the interventions. ... Of the 61 people who used the interventions, 39 consented to participate in the research project.' Entry to the analysed sample therefore required internal referral to the supported employment specialist, acceptance and USE of a vocational intervention, and consent. That is participation in a vocational service, which is employment-related selection under D9 irrespective of baseline employment status.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Recruitment, p. 116; Results, Overall engagement, p. 118. NOTE the selection here is NOT baseline employment status: 18 of the 39 (46 per cent) were in paid employment or full-time education at baseline and were offered the job-retention arm of the intervention, so the recruited sample spans both employed and unoccupied.

cohort_name: unnamed: Peking University Institute of Mental Health early-onset schizophrenia inpatient cohort, admissions of 2006
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10; primary clinical diagnosis at discharge of 'schizophrenia' (n = 113) or 'schizophrenia likely' (n = 5)
diagnosis_confirmed: 'Diagnoses were all made according to ICD-10 criteria by 2 or more experienced psychiatrists.' Diagnostic stability at follow-up was 76 per cent (42 of the 55 with information on subsequent diagnoses retained the schizophrenia diagnosis).
overlap_notes: Single centre, single admission year, patient records 14,001 to 15,000. No overlap with any other F13 cohort.
employment_selection_verbatim: 'Patient records numbered 14,001 to 15,000 were consecutively assessed, and subjects were enrolled according to the following criteria: 1. Patient's age did not reach 18 years old on day of admission. 2. Primary clinical diagnosis at discharge was "schizophrenia" (n = 113) or "schizophrenia likely" (n = 5) ... 3. Patients or family members have sufficient comprehension of Mandarin Chinese. A total of 118 patients were identified according to the above criteria and included in our study.' Three criteria, stated in full, none of them employment-related; employment is an outcome measured at follow-up, never an entry condition. The analysed denominator of 62 is the surviving interviewees and carries no employment restriction either.

cohort_name: unnamed: 13 Japanese supported employment programmes, JiSEF fidelity and service-process study, 2014-2015
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 diagnosis of schizophrenia, required at eligibility; the report does not say who made the diagnosis or how it was verified
diagnosis_confirmed: Not described beyond 'had been diagnosed as having schizophrenia on the basis of the ICD-10'.
overlap_notes: 13 of 25 agencies identified in the JiSEF scale-development research (Sasaki et al. 2018). Participants may overlap with the earlier Japanese pilot process study (Yamaguchi et al. 2017) and with the cognitive-remediation-plus-supported-employment RCT (Yamaguchi et al. 2017, Psychol Med); neither is held and neither is in this batch.
employment_selection_verbatim: 'The eligibility criteria were as follows: clients who were receiving employment services for the first time in each agency; had been diagnosed as having schizophrenia on the basis of the ICD-10; and were between ages 20 and 60 years.' Receiving employment services is the first eligibility criterion, so the whole cohort is defined by entry into a vocational service. This is a CRITICAL employment-related selection under D9 and bars the cohort from the primary prevalence pool however the outcome is coded.

cohort_name: Integrated Supported Employment randomised controlled trial, Wuxi Mental Health Center (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03273530)
diagnostic_instrument: Chinese version of the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV-TR (SCID); diagnosis of schizophrenia for at least 2 years required at entry
diagnosis_confirmed: 'The diagnosis of the participants was verified by the Chinese version of the Structural Clinical Interview (So, Kam, Leung, Pang, & Lam, 2003) for the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (4th ed., text rev.).'
overlap_notes: Two earlier pilot studies of the same ISE programme at the same centre are cited (Li et al. 2013; Lu et al. 2015). Neither is held; participant overlap is not stated and cannot be excluded.
employment_selection_verbatim: 'Inclusion criteria were as follows: (1) age 18 yr or older; (2) diagnosis of schizophrenia for at least 2 yr; (3) unemployed status; (4) willingness to give informed consent; (5) no obvious cognitive, learning, or neurological impairment as reflected in minimum scores on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE); (6) completion of primary school education; and (7) a desire to work.' TWO concurrent D9 triggers: criterion (3) is baseline employment status and criterion (7) is work intention or readiness. employment_selection_reason takes a single value and records the more objective of the two; the verbatim carries both.
